supported_evaluations.display_name: Financial reports: original vs single-pass aggregation
supported_evaluations.summary: Compare Sanchay's current three-pass report aggregation with a single-pass implementation over identical fictional ledgers.
supported_evaluations.change_summary: The Reports page currently walks the currency-scoped ledger three times: once for totals, once for category spending and once for payees. The candidate produces the same three results in one shared traversal.
supported_evaluations.mechanism: One pass accumulates minor-unit totals, category spending and payee amounts. The existing minor-unit money helpers and the existing ordering/filtering rules are retained.
correctness_rules: Totals, category breakdown and payee breakdown must match the original byte-for-byte after JSON canonicalisation.
Refunds reduce spending and payee totals exactly as the original does; they never become income.
Transfers are excluded from spending and payees; only completed goal debits count as saved.
Pending, failed and flagged transactions never contribute to a completed report.
Currencies are never combined; each report is scoped to one currency before aggregation.
JPY (zero minor digits) and two-decimal currencies keep their existing precision.
Results are deterministic and the original ledger array is not mutated.
supported_evaluations.scope_note: This evaluates a client-side report-calculation strategy. It does not evaluate API replicas, a server queue, PostgreSQL, or cloud failover, because Sanchay has no deployed server backend.
